title_guess: Repo rate, reverse repo rate and the Liquidity Adjustment Facility

segments.teaches: banks borrow from the RBI long-term at bank rate and short-term at repo rate; that cost passes into the loan rate people pay, so a lower rate means more borrowing

elements.what: bank icon -> 'loan' arrow -> person icon
central bank emblem coin above the letters RBI
blue side-barred label: banker of the banks
RBI -> loan splits into long term and short term, both arrows landing on the bank
cream strip holding two red % signs, pointed at by red labels bank rate and repo rate
dotted curved arrow carrying the repo % down to a % on the bank-to-person loan
loan % splits into less (red) / more (green), each with a small grey effect box on borrowing

segments.notes: Starts from the everyday case (bank lends to a person), then adds the layer above it. The % symbol is the recurring 'rate' token, always red.

segments.teaches: repo rate: RBI lends short-term to banks; reverse repo: banks lend short-term back to RBI; both are set by the RBI and act on banks' liquidity

elements.what: vertical chain RBI -> short-term loan -> repo % -> bank
dotted elbow loop from the bank back up to the RBI, labelled short-term loan sideways, with the reverse repo %
pale-blue bands with 'determined by RBI' over each rate label
bold 'liquidity' word on a blue underline beneath the bank, branching to low (red) and high (green)
italic definition of liquidity beside the bank

segments.notes: Two opposite-direction flows on one diagram: solid arrow down for repo, dotted loop up for reverse repo.

segments.teaches: lowering both rates raises liquidity; raising both rates lowers it

elements.what: words 'decreased' (green) inserted in both rate bands, later swapped to 'increased' (red)
small grey notes under low and high liquidity: both rates increased / both rates decreased

segments.notes: State-swap trick: the same labels flip from decreased to increased while the diagram stays still, showing the two policy directions.

segments.teaches: together the two rates form the Liquidity Adjustment Facility (from 2000), a key tool of RBI monetary policy

elements.what: the two % rates pulled together into one blue box with a thick black border
letter-spaced acronym LAF with full name under the box
yellow bracketed chip with the year introduced
purple letter-spaced line: key element of the monetary policy framework
dotted loop from the box down to liquidity

segments.notes: Grouping trick: separate items collapse into one framed box that is then named.

segments.teaches: repo is a repurchase agreement: the bank gives government securities to the RBI as collateral and promises to buy them back on a set date at a set price

elements.what: RBI -> short-term loan -> repo % -> bank (reverse loop removed)
bond certificate between bank and RBI, linked to a government-security label
national emblem used as the government icon
dotted loop bank -> security -> RBI
cream band laid across loan and security
checklist document (agreement)
speech box from the document with the repurchase promise, key word highlighted blue; curved arrow to a bold title 'repurchase agreement'

segments.notes: Explains the name of the instrument by unpacking the word (repo = repurchase).

segments.teaches: the RBI buys the security at a discount to its price; the discount is set by the repo rate; the buy-back price is the rate of repurchase

elements.what: arrow from the document down-left to a note: RBI buys at a discounted price
discounted price -> calculated from repo rate -> curved arrow to rate of repurchase
white value chips: security worth 100, loan given as 100 minus discount

segments.notes: Small running numeric example (100 vs 100 minus discount) placed directly on the diagram parts it describes.

segments.teaches: the basic repo is an overnight loan

elements.what: 'repurchase agreement' title moved beside the document
green ribbon-shaped banner 'repo' with a dashed border, led by an 'overnight' label

segments.notes: Canvas then holds still for about 80 seconds while the narrator talks; no visual change in that stretch.

segments.teaches: term repos (from 2013) last longer than overnight, usually 7, 14 or 28 days; long-term repos (LTRO, from 2020) run 1 to 3 years

elements.what: second green ribbon 'term repos' and a pink ribbon 'long term repos' stacked under the first
yellow sticky note with a paper clip: year and typical durations, linked by a line to 'longer than overnight'
second sticky note with the later year, plus the LTRO expansion and duration label

segments.notes: Ribbon stack + clipped sticky notes act as a mini timeline of when each repo type arrived.

segments.teaches: how much a bank can borrow: a set share of its deposits (NDTL); with deposits of 2000 crore, 0.25 percent and 0.75 percent give 5 and 15 crore

elements.what: the three ribbons moved to the top-left as a legend
clipped sticky note on the bank: NDTL 2000 crore
dash-chains from each ribbon: percent of NDTL -> amount in crore (blue)
sticky note under the LTRO ribbon with the total amount offered

segments.notes: Running numeric example: one assumed deposit base turned into borrowing limits for each repo type.

segments.teaches: reverse repo: banks park surplus funds with the RBI; the RBI gives securities and promises to buy them back; it is a reverse repurchase agreement

elements.what: dotted loop from bank up to RBI with reverse repo %, the repo chain fading away
tilted red-orange paper note over the bank: banks park surplus funds with RBI
dotted loop from RBI across to the security and down to the bank (opposite direction to repo)
cream band over the whole reverse flow
agreement speech box with 'resell' highlighted, titled reverse repurchase agreement
note: RBI sells securities at a discounted price

segments.notes: Mirror of the repo segment with arrows reversed and one key word changed; reuses the same component layout.

elements.what: next-video and playlist panels with illustrated birds
